apiKeys.title: App keys (API)
apiKeys.description: Connect your own app — a mobile app, for example — to this application. The key identifies your account and carries exactly the rights you give it.
apiKeys.offTitle: The HTTP API is switched off
apiKeys.offDisabledBody: This app does not currently offer an API for your own programs. Existing keys do not work — but you can still revoke them here.
apiKeys.offBrokenBody: The API's settings are broken, so it is switched off. Please contact the operator of this app.
apiKeys.noSelfServiceBody: This app does not hand out app keys on request. You can still revoke keys you already hold.
apiKeys.planRequiredBody: The HTTP API is not part of your access. You can still revoke keys you already hold.
apiKeys.endpointBody: Your program reaches the API at this address — together with the key from below in the Authorization header.
apiKeys.createDescription: The key is shown to you exactly once. After that nobody can read it back — not even the operator of this app.
apiKeys.nameHint: Just for you, so you can tell your keys apart.
apiKeys.scopeHint: A read-only key cannot change anything and cannot cost anything. Take it if you are not sure.
apiKeys.secretTitle: Your new key — copy it now
apiKeys.secretBody: This is the only time you get to see it. Copy it into your program now. If it gets lost, simply create a new one and revoke this one.
apiKeys.limitBody: More than {max} active keys is not possible — not as a restriction, but so the list stays manageable. Revoke one you no longer need.
apiKeys.emptyBody: Create a key to connect your own app to this application.
apiKeys.revokeBody: The program using this key is locked out immediately. This cannot be undone — but you can create a new key at any time.
apiKeys.accountExportNote: Your app keys: their name, their scopes and when each was last used. Not the key itself — it is held only as a hash and cannot be read back.
apiKeys.accountDeletionNote: Your app keys. Any program using one to reach your account loses its access immediately.

errors.apiNameRequired: Please give the key a name — otherwise you will not know later which one you can revoke.
errors.apiNameTooLong: That name is too long (60 characters at most).
errors.apiTooManyKeys: You already hold the maximum number of active keys. Revoke one you no longer need.
errors.apiUnknownKey: That key does not exist (any more).
errors.apiDisabled: This app does not currently offer an HTTP API.
errors.apiSelfServiceOff: This app does not hand out app keys on request.
errors.apiPlanRequired: The HTTP API is not part of your access.
